kindHint.npcs: A unique person exists once per game; an archetype as many times as the story needs.
kindHint.locations: A unique place exists once per game; an archetype stands for any place of its kind.
kindHint.items: A unique item exists once per game; an archetype as many times as the story needs.

descriptionHint: One line of English for the model, never shown to the player.

generic.npcs: Generic: stands for anyone the player runs into
generic.items: Generic: stands for anything the player picks up

combatHint: JSON: skills in percent by reference, hitPointsMax, the item reference of the ordinary weapon (or null), the damage modifier as the book gives it (+1D4, or null for none) and the ordinary armour (0 for none).
parentHint: The named place that contains this one, if any.
exitsHint: JSON list, empty for a place travelled to freely. Each exit leads to another named place (to), reads in one line of English from here (passage) and from the other side if it differs (backPassage, or null), may be hidden from this side, require an item to open (requires, or null), lead one way only (oneWay), and take moment, minutes, hour or hours (duration, or null for a moment). Declare a passage once, on one side: it leads both ways. Describe each side as it is seen from there, without naming what lies beyond — "a heavy door beside the stairs", not "the library door": the character learns what a room is by going in. An exit may also be blocked at some periods of the day, from either side (blockedDuring, a list of periods), with a line of English on why (blockedReason): no key and no skill opens it then.
entrance: Entrance: the network opens onto the places travelled to freely here
periodNotes: Notes for the time of day
periodNotesHint: JSON list, empty for none. Each note adds one line of English to the description at some periods of the day (periods, note). Like the description, it names no named person not met yet and nothing behind a passage.
stackable: Stackable: copies are interchangeable and counted by quantity
initialLocation: Waits when the game starts in
initialLocationHint: A named place; the person comes into being there, the first time the game visits it.
scheduleHint: JSON list, empty for none. Each entry sends the person to a named place (location) at some periods of the day (periods: dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, dusk, evening, night — each in one entry at most), with what they do there in one line of English (activity, or null), whether they leave the character's company to keep to it (leavesScene), and whether their arrival where the character is cuts a long action short (interrupts). A period no entry covers leaves them where they are; someone with a schedule is placed by it rather than by where they wait from the start.
initialHolder: Held when the game starts by
initialHolderHint: A named person or place; the item comes into being with them.
hidden: Hidden there: out of sight until a search finds it, like a hidden exit
modifiersHint: JSON list: each with target "skill", the skill, a value in percent (±20 for a tool of quality), condition (owned or equipped) and description.
weaponHint: JSON, empty for anything that is no weapon: what it is (melee, thrown or projectile — the attack's category names the skill), its damage dice (1D6+1), how much of the wielder's damage modifier it adds (full, half or none) and its special effect (bleeding, crushing, entangling, impaling, knockback, or null).
armorHint: What it stops of every blow while worn: 1 for a buff coat, 0 for anything that is no armour.

intro.npcs: The people the scene can hold. The model picks from this list and never invents someone with a state of their own.
intro.locations: The places of the world, named or generic. A movement names a named place, or a new place of an archetype.
intro.items: The items of the world. The model picks from this list and never makes up an item.
